Hi Lisa —

Appreciate the clear list. We can absolutely provide an operations attestation and a sample erasure artifact. High-level answers up front:

- Residency: For Private/VPC deployments, customer-controlled storage is bound to the region you request (us-east-1) and we do not replicate tenant data outside of your VPC by default. Any cross-region replication is opt-in and would require an explicit configuration change on your account.
- Deletion workflow: Tenant-initiated deletion triggers a multi-stage pipeline: logical remove -> background shredding of object storage + KV cache purge -> metadata sweep -> optional crypto-key rotation. Typical completion window is 24–72 hours for standard datasets; longer for queued inference caches.
- KMS: We support customer-provided KMS keys in dedicated private deployments (customer-managed keys). Keys remain under your KMS control; Redwood never stores the raw key material.

Would you like us to schedule a 30-min call with our Security Operations (Rishi) and Solutions (Marissa) to walk through a draft attestation and the sample artifacts? If so, propose a couple of times and I’ll coordinate. We’ll prepare a short PDF attestation and an example erasure CSV.

Thanks for the patience. Per Karthik's note, please find our operations-level attestation and a short Q&A that addresses each point in your spreadsheet. We’ve attached the formal attestation PDF and a sanitized erasure log sample. If this looks good we can provide a DocuSign-ready copy.

Executive attestation (summary):
- Residency guarantee: For private VPC deployments configured for us-east-1, Redwood Inference binds tenant storage and primary replicas to that region by default. We do not perform cross-region replication without explicit customer configuration.
- Deletion pipeline and evidence: Tenant delete requests initiate the following controlled process:
  1) Receive request (API or Console) — request acknowleged and assigned a job id.
  2) Logical delete — pointers/indices are removed immediately.
  3) Background purge — object store shredding and KV cache eviction proceed as background jobs.
  4) Metadata sweep — full metadata reconciliation and tombstone removal.
  5) Audit record generation — system records a hash and job status; evidence artifact generated (CSV/JSON).
  Typical completion window: 24–72 hours for ordinary workloads. For very large multi-TB datasets or queued requests the pipeline can take up to 7 days; we will include estimated duration in the attestation.
- KMS model: DataCore may provide customer-managed KMS keys. In this mode, Redwood holds only ciphertext; key material remains in your KMS. We provide guidance for CMK rotation and revocation and document the timeline for re-encrypting ephemeral caches.

Limitations & notes:
- In-flight inference caches stored on GPU hosts are best-effort scrubbed on tenant deletion; full cryptographic destruction may require instance reclamation which can take up to 48 hours depending on scaling schedules.
- If you enable optional cross-region backup, we will include region destinations in the attestation — by default this is off.

- erasure-log-sample.csv (sanitized example: job_id, object_id, timestamp_utc, operation, sha256_digest)
